brief: Elizabeth Fry was born in Norwich in 1780. She was a member of the Society of Friends, and her deep religious faith found a practical outlet in her lifelong commitment to prison reform. Her daily visits to women prisoners in Newgate gaol enabled her to see for herself the degradation they suffered. She began a campaign for reform, which was instrumental in bringing about change. She was also involved in the establishment of a “Nightly Shelter for the Homeless”, and before her death in 1845 she founded a society for the care and rehabilitation of former offenders.
